chapter: Later career, civil service and jazz seminars
title: Who plays in the seminar group and how a college seminar runs
summary: Caldwell takes Gene Rodgers, Tommy Benford and others; they play, announce each soloist and answer students' questions.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, just let's come back to this thing. You take -- you say you take Bernard Flood, yourself. Who else goes down to this seminar?
Oh, we take like this piano player -- oh, I take like Gene Rodgers. He made a recording with --
Is he still around? Coleman--
(Unintelligible) Gene about -- oh, I guess almost 15 years I ran into him around Doc Vollmer's there. He was -- when I looked at him --
Where does he live?
He lives in Long Island. He married, has a wife with him (unintelligible). He moved to -- he said, Happy Caldwell, he grabbed -- you (unintelligible), says --
Well, he's from Chicago, isn't he?
I think he's New York boy. Gene was a New York boy, quite sure.
Well, the only thing -- only mason I thought he was from Chicago was somebody told me he used to play sort of like intermission inhibition piano at the Grand Terrace.
Maybe he did.
Yeah, but he could be from New York. That's true.
He could be, yeah, because I know when I first met him, he had possibilities (unintelligible) maybe he was from Chicago.
And then you'd take Tommy Benford. Who would you take on bass?

Tommy -- I would take (unintelligible) bass, couldn't get George Dupvier, (unintelligible) but I'd take this other fellow there plays very good guitar and bass, and he does these things around these different colleges, writes and arranges, and he's got a well known name too in music.
What's his name?
His name is Wilson. I don't think he ever made the big top, but he's very good. He's always working.
Gene Rodgers, right, New York City.
Is that Gene Rodgers? Yeah, New York City.
Yeah. Well, then -- say, you go down and you play. And then what else?
You play and then students ask little questions. (unintelligible) certain (unintelligible).
Do you with each -- I mean if they want to know something about the piano, does Gene --
Yeah.
I see.

Then you announce each man. Each man going to have a solo, what they want to play. They announce him, and you get a few little highlights of his background, where he played with and where he was born. That's it, either one. And you go for the finale, play some jump numbers, if you want to play some ballads or something like that. Then the kids all know what you're doing. They know what you're doing.
Well, I mean are these kids music students, most of them?
Yeah.
They are.
You know, they have some good bands too there.
(Simultaneous remarks)
I once went to Fordham when they had Benny Morton --
Yes, Fordham.
-- Doc Cheatham and people like that.
That would be the same sort of thing.
Same thing.
Yeah. Well, what else are you doing nowadays?
Still making gigs, working on that part time anyway.
